content.body:
It had already been determined as early as the mid/late period of 1939 that a replacement for the Matilda II would be needed ... the crushing loss of the BEF in 1940 and almost all the equipment, tanks and guns then in British service …led to the crash development of the Churchill as a heavy tank to stem the anticipated German invasion.
The Churchill went on to become one of the most widely used British tanks of the war with dozens of variants employed in all theaters. Heavy armor virtually the equal of the German Tiger tank in many respects, coupled with a low silhouette made it a popular tank with its crews due to its survivability under fire, but its slow road speed and 6 pounder gun, when compared directly to German tank guns and the armour they were employing by this time ... always left it as wanting something more in terms of how it might ideally have been. In its defense it was one of the most unbeatable tanks of the war off road, being highly mobile in tight going or when climbing steep grades.
The Churchill should be played like a bigger, badder, better Matilda II: you should remain cautious about air attack because while your heavy armor all around will give you considerable security and time when you encounter enemy tanks ... the enemy tankers will very likely have called in heavy air support from their bombers to eliminate you. This IS going to happen no matter how often you pretend it isn't. Stukas are everywhere and they will find you.
The main threats you need to consider are the ubiquitous and ever present 88mm FlaK gun, and the Tiger tank which mounts an improved weapon in an extremely heavily armoured turret. Even though the Tiger usually enters the game world after the churchill III does, the long 75mm guns of the PzKw.IVg and StuG.IIIg can still put a hurt on the Churchill under the right circumstances. Your lack of speed will make maneuver tactics to flank enemy armour difficult, and it will always serve you better to use your low profile to act as an extremely nasty ambush tank; your armor allowing you to retreat or even advance under what could be very heavy enemy fire once they know where you are hiding. Try to keep a berm or terrain elevation between your tank and enemy fire as your tracks are as vulnerable as any other tracked vehicles tracks are, and the weak point of any tank no matter what kind it is.
The Churchill III, will be a prime target for enemy forces; be they tanks, bombers, AT guns or even anti-tank infantry. You must always assume you are the number one unit in the British armoured forces that the enemy wants to see killed in battle. The 6 pdr. gun is a good AT gun, firing a high velocity if somewhat light AT round. The Crusader III stable mate is armed with exactly the same gun, but being lighter and faster can make a good running partner doing the flanking work while the Churchill slugs it out at in the more normal, if highly dangerous frontal trade shots contest. The Churchill has good armour but it's opponents have great guns in their 75's, frontal slugfests are best left to the dead tankers that they will soon become.
